book: Philippe Cornu, Tibetan Astrology, Hamish Gregor English translation, Shambhala edition; two-up scanned PDF

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Cornu distinguishes the Chinese-derived Jungtsi dynamic Wood/Fire/Earth/Iron/Water agents from the Indian set of earth/water/fire/air/ether, cautioning that superficial analogies such as wood–air do not make the systems identical.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: The generative sequence is Wood→Fire→Earth→Metal→Water→Wood; the destructive cycle is Metal defeats Wood, Fire defeats Metal, Water defeats Fire, Earth defeats Water, Wood defeats Earth. Source identifies direction, so reversing an ordered relation is not equivalent.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Cornu ranks white/black pebble relations as mother (three white), friend (two white), Earth/Water identity (one white), son (white/black), Fire/Metal/Wood identity (one black), enemy (two black). These are traditional categories, not outcome observations.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: An element-year has active/passive or male/female polarity independent of an individual person's biological sex; the text illustrates masculine/feminine forms of each of five elements.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Twelve animal signs name Tibetan years, months, days and double-hours; calculations for the four positions are not interchangeable and need their respective calendar-derived time units.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: The source distinguishes five person-level forces: La (spirit), Sok (life/vitality), Lü (body/health), Wangthang (personal power), Lungta (wind-horse/fortune). Its traditional accounts of demons and remedies are cultural descriptions, not medical mechanisms.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Traditional natal vitality element depends on animal group: Tiger/Hare Wood; Horse/Snake Fire; Monkey/Bird Iron; Mouse/Pig Water; Ox/Sheep/Dog/Dragon Earth. These groups can be computed from a documented Tibetan year animal.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Windhorse element follows four compatible animal trines: Mouse/Dragon/Monkey Wood; Ox/Snake/Bird Water; Tiger/Horse/Dog Iron; Hare/Sheep/Pig Fire; there is no Earth windhorse trine in this scheme.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Annual changes in the five personal forces are evaluated by comparing current year elemental counterparts with natal year counterparts, including mother/son/identity/friend/enemy distinctions. Different axes must not be scored as independent individuals.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Cornu presents Kartsi as Indian-derived, primarily astronomical/zodiacal astrology, distinct from the Chinese-origin Naktsi/Jungtsi calendar-elemental systems; merging shared representations would erase method boundaries.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Kartsi describes 27 lunar mansions (gyukar) and also mentions 28 constellation guardians; the 27 equal lunar zodiac divisions used for chart calculation should not be confused with the set of 28 named star groups.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: In Cornu's Tibetan counting, 27 mansions are numbered from 0 through 26, contrasting Indian 1–27 indexing; any software crosswalk must specify zero- versus one-based convention.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: For natal gyukar, first interpolate Moon's tropical geocentric longitude at birth, then subtract a declared ayanāṃśa and map into sidereal mansion sectors. Solar-year approximation and precise astronomical ephemeris are distinct choices.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: The instructional calculation uses a coincidence epoch near CE285 and annual precession of 0.014 degrees, a historical approximation rather than a universally endorsed modern sidereal zero-point.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: The author demonstrates planetary and lunar-mansion classifications on an illustrative 1957 chart; assertions about long life, accidents and powers are textual predictions, not observed or validated outcomes.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: The Tibetan-day chapter separates general auspicious days for specific activities from personal days assessed relative to someone's natal features; neither should be treated as an independent birth-only personality prediction.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Cornu's day uses twelve animal-named double-hours starting with Hare around 05:00–07:00 (local solar daypart); the entire time convention including historical timezone/summer offset must be fixed before converting a timestamp.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Hour elements start with the son of the lunar day element for Hare, then progress through the generating five-element sequence at every succeeding double-hour. Worked Water Dragon day: Hare Wood, Dragon Fire, Snake Earth, Horse Metal, Sheep Water.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: The book's Paris example dated 15 November 1950, 17:00 civil time, is placed on Tibetan month 10 day 6, Iron Tiger year, Monkey hour, with Water Ox month, Wood Ox day, Fire Monkey hour; this is one authored chart, not independently validated astronomy.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: For the same Iron Tiger natal year the author gives vitality Wood, body Wood, power Iron, fortune Iron, and La Water; this is a source-level numerical illustration agreeing structurally with Janson's later year-element formulas.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: For the same year the text gives Yellow Five natal/body mewa, Black Two vitality mewa and White Eight power mewa, with Black Two luck mewa. Its natal day 6 is Blue Three after natal day 1 Red Seven.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Cornu labels 17:00 Paris civil time minus one hour as 'local solar time' (16:00), then on p219 calls 16:09 'GMT'. Under the historical Paris UTC+1 rule and Paris longitude, these are UTC and local mean solar time respectively; the labels are reversed or conflated, so the worked planetary angles require independent recomputation.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Printed page 220 gives (1950−285)×0.014 = 23.31 = 23°81′. This last value is invalid sexagesimal minute notation; 23.31 decimal degrees instead equals 23°18′36″. Do not silently interpret 23°81′ as a permissible angle.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

notes.source_part: Part II practical astrology, book chapters 4–10
notes.paraphrase: Cornu's interpretive hierarchy gives natal year animal broad character, month more weight to element, and natal hour more weight to animal; the example's 12-factor element count is Wood4/Fire2/Earth2/Metal3/Water1, a descriptive scheme rather than calibrated probability.
notes.kind: modern instructional source statement, not classical Tibetan original nor empirical case

witness_method: Chapter passages independently examined in supplied PDF text; source arithmetic and key diagrams verified from page images. Excerpts and conclusions bounded to listed pages; NOT all Cornu text yet read.
overlap: Jungtsi year animals, windhorse trines, sidereal sky positions, and calendrical ideas overlap Chinese BaZi and Indian Jyotish. Multiple books sharing them are NOT independent human confirmations.
scope_warnings: Cornu translated year 'male/female' is sexagenary polarity; cannot assume person's sex.
1950 worked civil→UTC/LMT labels are internally inconsistent; use historical timezone database, not Cornu result as UTC golden until independently verified.
Printed 23°81′ is not a valid angular coordinate; decimal result 23.31° is coherent.
Traditional diagnostic, mortality and ritual claims are not clinical or human predictive evidence.
